---
title: HTML output
description: Configure accessible balloons or native tooltips in Quarto websites.
---

## Definition balloons

Balloon mode is the default:

```yaml
glossary:
  html-definition-display: balloon
```

References receive keyboard focus, a visible focus outline, and an accessible
label containing the term and definition. The bundled dependency-free helper
creates one popup under the document body and positions it near the active
reference.

This design preserves the scrolling and clipping behavior of source
containers. It works when [[metadata]] appears inside:

- callouts;
- responsive table cells;
- table captions;
- columns and cards; and
- containers with `overflow: auto` or `overflow: hidden`.

Press <kbd>Escape</kbd> to dismiss an open balloon. Moving focus or the
pointer away also closes it.

## Browser or Quarto tooltips

To use a native `title`-based tooltip instead:

```yaml
glossary:
  html-definition-display: tooltip
```

Tooltip mode omits the balloon JavaScript and data attributes. The two modes
are exclusive, preventing duplicate definition surfaces.

## Links and list anchors

With `link: true`, a reference links to its entry in a generated list. The link
is only created when that entry exists: on the same page, or on the page named
by `html-glossary-page`. A page with no list gets focusable, unlinked terms
that still show their definitions, so readers never follow a link to nothing.

Set `link: false` to turn links off everywhere:

```yaml
glossary:
  link: false
```

## Slides and other formats

Reveal.js slides are HTML, so balloons work there too. Word and Typst output
get plain references and the generated lists, with links when the document has
a list to point at.

## Styling

The extension deliberately uses Bootstrap-compatible color variables so it
adapts to Quarto light and dark themes. Override the popup narrowly in project
CSS when required:

```css
.glossary-balloon-popup {
  max-width: min(36rem, calc(100vw - 1rem));
}
```

Do not restore a `::after` balloon on `.glossary-term`; pseudo-elements are
trapped by overflowing callouts and responsive tables.
